artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let r be a positive integer and let F_q denote the finite field with q = 3^r elements, viewed as an abelian group under addition (equivalently, as the vector space F_3^r). A subset A ⊆ F_q is called progression-free (or a cap set) if it contains no three-term arithmetic progression, i.e., no three distinct elements x, y, z ∈ A with x + z = 2y (equivalently, since the characteristic is 3, no three distinct elements summing to 0). Denote by f(r) the maximum size of a progression-free subset of F_q.

It is known that f(r) ≤ 2·3^r / r (Meshulam) and that f(r) ≥ (2.217...)^r (Edel).

Address the following:
(a) Improve Meshulam's bound by showing that every progression-free subset A ⊆ F_q satisfies |A| = o(3^r / r).
(b) Determine whether there exists an absolute constant c < 3 such that f(r) ≤ c^r for all sufficiently large r.
(c) More generally, determine the asymptotic growth rate of f(r) as r → ∞.
artifact.status_search_result: Parts (a) and (b) were resolved in 2016 by Croot–Lev–Pach and Ellenberg–Gijswijt, who used the polynomial/slice rank method to show every progression-free subset of F_3^r has size O(c^r) with c ≈ 2.756 < 3, hence in particular o(3^r/r). The exact asymptotic growth rate (part c)—the precise value of the limit of f(r)^{1/r}, which lies between 2.2174 (Edel) and 2.756 (Ellenberg–Gijswijt)—remains open as of recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: On large subsets of F_q^n with no three-term arithmetic progression
status_evidence.snippet: Ellenberg and Gijswijt prove that a subset of F_3^n with no three-term AP has size at most O(2.756^n).
status_evidence.claim: The existence of c<3 with f(r) ≤ c^r was established.

status_evidence.title: Cap set - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: As of March 2023 there is no exponential improvement to Ellenberg and Gijswijt's upper bound; lower bound remains (2.2174)^n by Edel.
status_evidence.claim: The precise exponential growth rate of f(r) is still not determined.

status_evidence.title: Improved explicit upper bounds for the Cap Set Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Improvements to the explicit constants in the Ellenberg–Gijswijt cap set bound.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work has refined constants but not closed the gap with the lower bound.
